comment: NIM `part_of` fixture — the R3 relabel of the `include` row, pinned in BOTH directions. `include helpers` is a TEXTUAL scope-sharing inclusion (the included file's declarations join THIS module's single declaration space; no module is created and nothing can `import` what was included), which is the `part_of` contract (src/ast/types.ts:164-190). The relabel is 1:1: same source `(global)`, same target `helpers` (the analyzer's normalized MODULE NAME), same line, same confidence, same `metadata.relationshipType: "nim_include"` marker. Two metadata fields are the contract's: `partRole: "library"` — nim has only the host role of Dart's two, because an included file does not know it is included — and `targetResolution: "module-name"`, which RECORDS the divergence from fsharp/php (they emit project-relative paths) rather than flattening it. The forbid half is what stops a half-relabel: a row emitted under BOTH labels would double-count in the closure, and the old label would still be published.

expectRelationships.comment: the relabel: `include helpers` is a part_of row from the file carrying the directive to the module name it names, with the mandatory partRole and the recorded target rule
the included declaration is callable from the including module — the scope-sharing half of the part_of semantics, and the reason `include` is not `imports`

forbidRelationships.comment: THE NEGATIVE HALF: the `include` row must no longer be published as `imports`. A relabel that emits both labels double-counts the construct and keeps the old spelling alive

expectImports.comment: the ImportInfo payload STAYS: it is the parsed directive list (persisted into brain_import by src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts), not a relationship, so a consumer reading the file's directive list loses nothing when the relationship's label moves
